messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content: At a pressure of about 10 kPa (roughly 0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water drops slightly below the normal 0 °C.  In practice it’s around **–2 °C** (≈ –3.6 °F).  This is because the solid phase of water is less dense than the liquid, so lowering the pressure shifts the melting/freezing equilibrium to lower temperatures.
